item.research_question: How can 2D layered high-entropy transition metal hydroxides with homogeneous elemental distribution and designed equimolar stoichiometry be synthesized via a bottom-up soft chemistry method?
item.material_system: High-entropy transition metal hydroxides (HEHs) with compositions (Co, Cr, Fe, Mn, Ni, Zn) in equimolar ratios, specifically HEH-1# (CoCrFeMnNi) and HEH-5# (CoFeMnNiZn)
item.processing_route: Solvothermal polyol process using ethylene glycol (EG) as solvent, metal nitrate/chloride salts, potassium acetate (KOAC) and/or NaOH as mineralizers, heated at 200 °C for 2 h; post-annealing in air at 200–1000 °C for 2 h with a heating rate of 2 °C min−1
item.test_conditions: Electrochemical OER testing in 0.1 M KOH electrolyte at 25 °C using a three-electrode system; magnetic measurements via SQUID at 2 K and 300 K; XRD, TEM, EDS, FT-IR, TG-DTA, and ICP-MS characterization
key_findings: Interlayer distances of as-synthesized 2D HEHs range from 0.860 to 0.987 nm under EG-K/N conditions.
HEH-5# (CoFeMnNiZn) synthesized under EG-K/N conditions exhibits an overpotential of 275 mV at 10 mA cm−2 for the oxygen evolution reaction.
Annealing at 200 °C converts 2D HEHs into spinel-type nanoparticles with a size of 5 nm and specific surface area of 242.0 m2 g−1.
600 °C-annealed HEH nanoparticles exhibit superparamagnetic behavior with a blocking temperature of 245 K.
Under EG-K/N conditions, all five metal elements are uniformly distributed in the layered structures with no obvious elemental segregation.
The HEH-5# EG-K/N sample shows better OER performance than HEH-1# due to the substitution of Cr with Zn.
Annealing above 200 °C reduces OER activity due to the collapse of layered structures and increased crystallinity.
item.mechanism: The polyol process involves hydrolysis and inorganic polymerization of metal-containing species in ethylene glycol media; the presence of OH− and acetate ions facilitates complexation with metal cations, while the EG solvent inhibits elemental segregation. The formation of high-entropy inorganic–organic hybrid compounds (metal hydroxide acetates) allows co-precipitation of multiple cations at the nanoscale, stabilizing the 2D layered structure. Post-annealing induces decomposition of organic groups and transformation into spinel-type oxides, where entropy stabilization and multi-element synergistic effects contribute to magnetic and catalytic properties.
item.limitations: High temperature (>230 °C) or pH (>13) leads to reduction of metal cations by ethylene glycol. The stoichiometry of as-synthesized products can deviate from design if pH is not controlled (e.g., Mn content is lower in EG-K conditions). Some irregularly shaped particles are observed, warranting further optimization of synthesis conditions.
item.future_work: Further study is required to understand the composition-metal species-magnetic property relationship and to optimize synthesis conditions to eliminate irregular particles. The work opens avenues for synthesizing other low-dimensional functional high-entropy materials such as spinel, pyrochlore, fluorite, perovskite oxides, and layered double hydroxides.
quotes: Here, we report a simple polyol process for the synthesis of a series of 2D layered high-entropy transition metal (Co, Cr, Fe, Mn, Ni, and Zn) hydroxides (HEHs)

The as-synthesized HEHs demonstrate 2D layered structures with interlayer distances ranging from 0.860 to 0.987 nm and homogeneous elemental distribution of designed equimolar stoichiometry in the layers.
These 2D HEHs exhibit a low overpotential of 275 mV at 10 mA cm−2 in a 0.1 M KOH electrolyte for the oxygen evolution reaction.
